skills.skill: Finding the least squares regression line
ti: Lists & Spreadsheet: enter the EV and RV in named lists (e.g. height, weight).
Add Data & Statistics: EV on the horizontal axis, RV on the vertical axis (turn Diagnostics on in Settings to show r²).
Menu › Analyze › Regression › Show Linear (a+bx): the line and its equation appear on the plot.
Write the equation in the variable names, e.g. weight = −84.8 + 0.867 × height.
classpad: Statistics app: enter the EV in list1 and the RV in list2 (or name the columns).
SetGraph: Scatter, XList = EV, YList = RV; tap the graph icon to draw the scatterplot.
Calc › Regression › Linear Reg; XList = EV, YList = RV; OK shows a, b, r, r²; OK again draws the line.
Write the equation in the variable names, e.g. weight = −84.8 + 0.867 × height.
skills.tip: Always check which variable is the EV before you start: “predict y from x” means x is the EV.

skills.skill: Making predictions from the regression line
ti: Find the least squares line (see lsrl); the line is stored as f1(x).
Calculator page: type f1(value of EV), e.g. f1(5), and press enter; or substitute by hand into the equation.
classpad: Find the least squares line (see lsrl), with the formula copied to y1.
Main app: type y1(value of EV), e.g. y1(5), and press EXE; or substitute by hand into the equation.
skills.tip: Check the EV value is inside the range of the data (interpolation) or outside it (extrapolation: unreliable).

ti: Draw the scatterplot and the least squares line (see lsrl).
Menu › Analyze › Residuals › Show Residual Plot (Hide Residual Plot to remove it).
Residual = actual − predicted: read the residual for a point, or calculate it from the equation.
classpad: Calc › Regression › Linear Reg with Copy Residual: list3 (the residuals are stored in list3).

skills.tip: Random scatter around 0 supports linearity; a clear pattern (e.g. a curve) means the association is not linear.

skills.skill: Fitting a regression line to transformed data
ti: Lists & Spreadsheet: enter the data in named lists (e.g. lifespan, gdp).
Name a new column for the transformed variable (e.g. lgdp) and in its formula cell type =log(gdp) (or =gdp^2, =1/gdp).
Add Data & Statistics: plot the RV against the transformed variable (check the plot is now linear).
Menu › Analyze › Regression › Show Linear (a+bx). The x in the equation is the transformed variable.
Write the equation in the variable names, e.g. lifespan = 54.3 + 5.59 × log(GDP); substitute to predict (undo a log y or 1/y at the end).
classpad: Statistics app: enter the data in named lists (e.g. Lifespan, GDP).
Name a third list (e.g. logGDP) and in its calculation cell at the bottom type log(GDP) (or GDP^2, 1/GDP).
SetGraph: Scatter, XList = transformed list, YList = RV; draw it and check the plot is linear.
Calc › Regression › Linear Reg with the same lists: read a, b, r²; the x is the transformed variable.
Write the equation in the variable names; substitute to predict (undo a log y or 1/y at the end).
skills.tip: Transform only one variable. If you transformed y, the answer from the equation is log y, y² or 1/y: undo it (10^, √, 1/) to get the prediction.

skills.skill: Checking a transformation: residual plot and r²
ti: Make a column for each transformation to try (x², log x, 1/x or y², log y, 1/y) as in "Fitting a regression line to transformed data".
For each one: Data & Statistics plot, Show Linear (a+bx), turn on Diagnostics to show r².
Menu › Analyze › Residuals › Show Residual Plot: look for no clear pattern.
Choose the transformation with the patternless residual plot and the highest r².
classpad: Make a list for each transformation to try (e.g. x², log x, 1/x).
For each one: Calc › Regression › Linear Reg (XList = transformed list) and read r².
Set Copy Residual to a list, then plot residuals against the transformed list as a scatterplot: look for no clear pattern.
Choose the transformation with the patternless residual plot and the highest r².
skills.tip: Use the circle of transformations first to pick the candidates, then let r² and the residual plot decide.

classpad.title: ClassPad Help 412 – xyLine time series

skills.checked: Cambridge U3&4 5A CAS 1 + Edrolo 4A WE1 (Draft, check against 02 Sources\CAS guides)

ti: Lists & Spreadsheet: enter the time (1, 2, 3 …) in column A (name it e.g. day) and the values in column B (e.g. rainfall).
Three-mean: in cell C2 type =(b1+b2+b3)/3 and press enter (C1 stays blank: no smoothed value for the first point).
Select C2, drag its bottom-right corner down to the second-last row to copy the formula.
Five-mean: start in C3 with =(b1+b2+b3+b4+b5)/5 and copy down to the third-last row.
With centring (even n): two-mean start in C2 with =(b1+2b2+b3)/4; four-mean start in C3 with =(b1+2b2+2b3+2b4+b5)/8; copy down as before.
classpad: Spreadsheet app: enter the time (1, 2, 3 …) in column A and the values in column B.
Three-mean: select C2, type =(B1+B2+B3)/3 and press EXE (C1 stays blank).
Select C2 and drag down to the second-last row to copy the formula.
Five-mean: start in C3 with =(B1+B2+B3+B4+B5)/5 and copy down to the third-last row.
With centring (even n): two-mean start in C2 with =(B1+2B2+B3)/4; four-mean start in C3 with =(B1+2B2+2B3+2B4+B5)/8; copy down as before.
skills.tip: An n-mean (n odd) loses (n − 1) ÷ 2 points at each end. Round only the final smoothed values. Centred n-mean (n even) also loses n ÷ 2 points at each end.

skills.skill: Generating a sequence from a recurrence relation
ti: Calculator page: type the starting value (e.g. 300) and press enter.
Type the rule using the previous answer, e.g. ×0.5 − 9 (the calculator shows ans·0.5−9), and press enter.
Keep pressing enter: each press gives the next term (V₁, V₂, V₃ …). Count the presses to name the term.
classpad: Main application: type the starting value (e.g. 300) and press EXE.
Type the rule using ans, e.g. ans × 0.5 − 9, and press EXE.
Keep pressing EXE: each press gives the next term (V₁, V₂, V₃ …). Count the presses to name the term.
skills.tip: The starting value is V₀, so the first press of enter/EXE after typing the rule gives V₁.
skills.checked: Cambridge U3&4 7A Examples 3, 5 + Edrolo 5A WE5 (Draft, check against 02 Sources\CAS guides)

skills.skill: Solving a geometric growth/decay rule for n or r
ti: Calculator page: Menu › Algebra › Solve.
Enter the rule with the known values, e.g. solve(8000 = 1.06^n × 5000, n) or solve(15000 = (1 − r/100)^10 × 56000, r), and press enter.
n: round UP to the next whole period. r: keep the sensible solution (between 0 and 100) and round as asked.
classpad: Main application: Action › Advanced › solve (or type solve( from the keyboard).
Enter the rule with the known values, e.g. solve(8000 = 1.06^n × 5000, n) or solve(15000 = (1 − r/100)^10 × 56000, r), and press EXE.
n: round UP to the next whole period. r: keep the sensible solution (between 0 and 100) and round as asked.
skills.tip: Write the rule Vₙ = Rⁿ × V₀ first, then substitute; there are often two solutions for r.
skills.checked: Cambridge U3&4 7E Examples 26, 27 (Draft, check against 02 Sources\CAS guides)

ti: Calculator page: Menu › Finance › Interest Conversion › Effective Interest Rate (pastes eff( ).
Enter eff(nominal rate, compounding periods per year), e.g. eff(4.5, 12), and press enter.
Write the effective rate as a percentage, rounded as asked (e.g. 4.594%).
classpad: Main application: Interactive › Financial › Interest Conversion › convEff.
Enter the compounding periods per year (e.g. 12) and the nominal rate (e.g. 4.5); OK.
Write the effective rate as a percentage, rounded as asked (e.g. 4.594%).
skills.tip: The effective rate is always higher than the nominal rate when interest compounds more than once a year.
skills.checked: Cambridge U3&4 7F Example 32 + Edrolo 5G WE1 (Draft, check against 02 Sources\CAS guides)

skills.skill: Entering and storing a matrix (and its transpose)
ti: Calculator page: press the template key (beside 9) and choose the m × n matrix template; enter the number of rows and columns; OK.
Type the elements, using tab to move between them.
Store it: press ctrl var (sto→), type a letter (e.g. a) and press enter.
Transpose: type a then Menu › Matrix & Vector › Transpose (shows aᵀ) and press enter.
classpad: Main application: open the Keyboard › Math2 tab and tap the matrix template; tap the add-row / add-column buttons until the order is right.
Type the elements, tapping each cell.
Store it: tap ⇒ and type a letter (e.g. A), then EXE.
Transpose: Action › Matrix › Create › trn, type trn(A) and press EXE.
skills.tip: Check the order (rows × columns) on screen before storing; a stored letter keeps its matrix until you overwrite it.
skills.checked: Cambridge U3&4 10A CAS 1 + Edrolo 7B WE3 (Draft, check against 02 Sources\CAS guides)

skills.skill: Matrix arithmetic: sum, difference, scalar multiple, product and power
ti: Enter and store each matrix (see Entering and storing a matrix).
Type the calculation with the stored letters, e.g. a+b, a−b, 3·a, a·b (use ×) or a^2, and press enter.
"Error: Dimension" means the operation is not defined for those orders.
classpad: Enter and store each matrix (see Entering and storing a matrix).
Type the calculation with the stored letters, e.g. A+B, A−B, 3A, A×B or A^2, and press EXE.
"Dimension ERROR" means the operation is not defined for those orders.
skills.tip: Order matters for products: a·b and b·a are usually different (or one is not defined).
skills.checked: Cambridge U3&4 10C CAS 2, 10D CAS 3-4 + Edrolo 7B WE2, 7C WE2 Method 2 (Draft, check against 02 Sources\CAS guides)

skills.skill: Determinant and inverse of a matrix; solving AX = B
ti: Enter and store the matrix (e.g. as a).
Determinant: Menu › Matrix & Vector › Determinant, type det(a) and press enter.
Inverse: type a^-1 and press enter ("Singular matrix" means det = 0, no inverse).
Solve AX = B: type a^-1·b (pre-multiply); for XA = B type b·a^-1.
classpad: Enter and store the matrix (e.g. as A).
Determinant: Action › Matrix › Calculation › det, type det(A) and press EXE.
Inverse: type A^-1 and press EXE (an error means det = 0, no inverse).
Solve AX = B: type A^-1×B (pre-multiply); for XA = B type B×A^-1.
skills.tip: Find det first: if it is 0 the matrix has no inverse.
skills.checked: Cambridge U3&4 10E CAS 5 + Edrolo 7D WE1b, WE2 (Draft, check against 02 Sources\CAS guides)

skills.skill: Finance solver (TVM): loans, annuities, investments, perpetuities
ti: Calculator page: Menu › Finance › Finance Solver.
Enter N (number of payments), I(%) (annual rate), PV, Pmt, FV, PpY and CpY (payments/compounding per year; tab down). Money paid out by the person is negative, money received is positive.
Leave the unknown, move the cursor to it and press enter to solve. Read it off and round as asked (round N up to whole payments).
classpad: Main menu › Financial › Compound Interest.
Enter N, I%, PV, PMT, FV, P/Y and C/Y (End of period payments). Money paid out by the person is negative, money received is positive.
Tap the button of the unknown (N, I%, PV, PMT or FV) to solve it. Read it off and round as asked (round N up to whole payments).
skills.tip: Loan: PV +, Pmt −. Investment/annuity: PV −, Pmt + (annuity) or − (additions). Interest-only loan or perpetuity: FV = −PV.
skills.checked: Cambridge U3&4 8E–8I Examples 18–32 + Edrolo 6A WE2 (Draft, check against 02 Sources\CAS guides)
